purpose: Quantify magnitude representation error for a hypothetical proportional encoder; no SNN dynamics, training, decoder or format is selected.

source.access: read-only mmap of existing local SSD tensor; no copy or download

sampling.row_weighting: equal type weight, no corpus frequencies

assumptions: Each row is divided by its own largest absolute coordinate; its original signs and scale are preserved externally for comparison.
This is a shape-preserving diagnostic normalization, not the adopted SNN input encoder or runtime per-token scale.
Unsigned magnitudes use the full code range; phase state is excluded. FP4/FP8 retain their ordinary element sign-bit encodings, using only nonnegative values.
FP4/FP8 elements follow OCP MX v1.0 section 5.3, but this probe uses a real-valued row scale, not the MX block scale or block layout.
Ties are rounded to even; accumulation uses Python binary64.
Ideal population cases show attainable unweighted sum resolution if cell contributions can be balanced. They do not preserve individual learned outputs automatically.
No recurrence, cancellation, noise, phase transition, synaptic weight quantization, runtime speed or downstream semantic task is assessed.
